question: How stable are method rankings when an agent screens on a fraction of its training data? Assess the same classifiers at two training sizes on precisely the same 256 connected-group held rows. This is a retrospective diagnostic on a previously inspected development split, not an unseen benchmark.
candidates: Include every successful primary-split classifier with exactly identical executable parameter records in both runs and a retained small classifier. Match using a deterministic parameter-content hash, never score, name, or rank. Seal source joblib files and row order before scoring. Report every omission.
rows: Use the same pre-existing 256 development rows. Prove their connected-title groups do not intersect either model's fitting data, and that small fitting rows occur within large fitting rows. Match full archived predictions to the very same input tuples and indices. Use frozen unsupervised per-text feature caches for prediction only. No new fits, no API, no designated validation, official test, or H2.
measures: Report the original small internal search-order ranking, each small model's accuracy on the common 256, each large model's accuracy on exactly those 256, and complete primary-fold accuracy for context. Order tied accuracy by deterministic executable hash and also report all tied rank-one models. Compare average-tie Spearman rank correlations. Calculate 1000 paired group bootstrap rank correlations for common-row comparisons and top-1 regret by counting correct answers. These are descriptive sensitivity intervals.
decision: A small-first shortlist is a candidate for a future controlled scheduler trial only if common-row rank correlation exceeds 0.60 AND the three highest small common-row models include a large common-row leader. Separately disclose whether the actionable three highest original small search models would retain a large leader. This single post-hoc population does not authorize pruning in the shipped controller.
